extracted.intended_audience: aspiring naturalists, scientists, and general readers interested in scientific practice
extracted.subtask_description: Practical principles and habits for doing natural-history fieldwork, collecting specimens, geological mapping, and organising observations as described in a scientific autobiography. Emphasis on observation, record-keeping, verification, and intellectual habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect specimens and mark stratification on a map
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring back specimens of the rocks and to mark the stratification on a map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sedgwick often sent me on a line parallel to his, telling me to bring back specimens of the rocks and to mark the stratification on a map. (Practical instruction for making geologicalwork useful: collect physical samples and record their spatial/stratigraphic context.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough local observation to avoid overlooking conspicuous phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: It is easy to overlook phenomena, however conspicuous, before they have been observed by any one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: at Cwm Idwal neither Darwin nor Sedgwick noticed obvious glacial phenomena (scored rocks, perched boulders, moraines) until later recognized. Anti-pattern: assuming absence because you failed to observe; maintain vigilance and develop frameworks to see phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct traverses and field routes tailored to investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Traverse country by compass and map, following a straight line unless a track coincides with the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical field method Darwin used to encounter 'strange wild places' and ensure coverage of unexplored ground rather than sticking to existing paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop drawing and anatomical skills for specimen descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Inability to draw, and insufficient anatomical knowledge, made much MS. produced during the voyage almost useless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/anti-pattern: collect and describe specimens, but without drawing/anatomical skill the notes may be of limited value. Invest in skills that allow clear depiction and anatomical understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a careful, vivid journal describing observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the Journal daily, describing carefully and vividly all that I had seen; this was good practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Journal also served as letters and provided source material for later publications. Good practice: detailed, vivid daily records aid later synthesis and communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record stratification and fossils at many points; reason and predict
rubrics_metrics.description: By recording the stratification and nature of the rocks and fossils at many points, always reasoning and predicting what will be found elsewhere, the structure of the whole becomes intelligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological prescription for making order out of geological 'chaos': combine repeated local records with reasoning/prediction to infer regional structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study leading literature but retain critical judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: I had brought with me the first volume of Lyell's 'Principles of Geology,' which I studied attentively... Henslow advised me to get and study it but on no account to accept the views therein advocated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: use influential works to frame observations and methods, but avoid uncritical acceptance—study, then test by observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energetic industry and concentrated attention to current work
rubrics_metrics.description: The habit of energetic industry and of concentrated attention to whatever I was engaged in... Everything about which I thought or read was made to bear directly on what I had seen or was likely to see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intellectual habit emphasized as foundational to doing successful science: focus, connect reading/thinking directly to observations, sustain industry during projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work on Baconian principles: collect facts without preconceived theory
rubrics_metrics.description: I worked on true Baconian principles, and without any theory collected facts on a wholesale scale, more especially with respect to domesticated productions, by printed enquiries, by conversation with skilful breeders and gardeners, and by extensive reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic empirical data collection from many sources (surveys, correspondence, experts, literature) before building theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify deductive theories by careful observation
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole theory [of coral-reefs] was thought out... before I had seen a true coral reef. I had therefore only to verify and extend my views by a careful examination of living reefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine deductive/model-building with empirical verification: devise theory, then seek targeted observations to confirm or refute it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reliance on the principle of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: My paper was a great failure... my error has been a good lesson to me never to trust in science to the principle of exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: explaining phenomena simply because alternatives seem impossible under current knowledge. Be cautious and seek positive supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organise and index facts and references carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Buckle ... bought all the books which he read, and made a full index, to each, of the facts which he thought might prove serviceable... he could always remember in what book he had read anything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recommendation for scholars: maintain detailed indices and organized notes to retrieve supporting facts and references efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share specimens and results with specialists for appraisal
rubrics_metrics.description: My collection of fossil bones, which had been sent to Henslow, also excited considerable attention amongst palaeontologists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: send important collections to experts; collaboration and peer feedback can validate and publicize findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value minuteness and perfect accuracy in observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Robert Brown ... chiefly remarkable for the minuteness of his observations, and their perfect accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific virtue: precise, detailed observation is highly valuable even if it focuses on minute points; accuracy avoids later loss of knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate scientific temper: clearness, caution, sound judgment, candour
rubrics_metrics.description: Lyell's mind was characterised by clearness, caution, sound judgment, and a good deal of originality... His candour was highly remarkable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traits to emulate in scientific work: rigorous critical thinking, openness to objections, willingness to revise views, and generous engagement with others' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit errors, learn from failures, and avoid hubris
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper was a great failure, and I am ashamed of it... my error has been a good lesson to me...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-guidance: record and reflect on failed explanations; use mistakes as lessons to refine methods and avoid repeating overconfident inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed morphological/taxonomic work and careful description
rubrics_metrics.description: In my work on the Cirripedia I made out the homologies of the various parts... discovered the cementing apparatus... and proved the existence in certain genera of minute males complemental to and parasitic on the hermaphrodites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: undertake painstaking dissections, homology assessments, and clear descriptive work to support broader theoretical claims (importance illustrated by later use in classification and Origin of Species).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain correspondence and use printed enquiries to gather data
rubrics_metrics.description: Collected facts ... by printed enquiries, by conversation with skilful breeders and gardeners, and by extensive reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical data-gathering strategies: solicit information via printed enquiries, interview practitioners/breeders, and exhaust existing literature to amass empirical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance ambition with disinterested collection of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: I worked to the utmost during the voyage from the mere pleasure of investigation, and from my strong desire to add a few facts to the great mass of facts in Natural Science. But I was also ambitious ... I have never turned one inch out of my course to gain fame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative point: personal ambition may motivate work, but highest-quality science arises from sincere interest in facts rather than tailoring results for fame or public acclaim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise practical constraints (health, skills) on scientific productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: I was occasionally unwell, and so lost some time... my health almost always suffered from the excitement... I was compelled for many years to give up all dinner-parties ... I was enabled to resume work after hydropathic treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: plan for and mitigate health and life circumstances; acknowledge how practical constraints affect the pace and form of scientific work.
